dispute.idea_description: A minimal, intentionally trivial example repository published by GitHub itself and used to teach first-time users the basic fork -> clone -> edit -> push workflow, distinct from any real application code -- the content is deliberately a placeholder greeting or fork-prompt, not functional software.
dispute.ranking_rationale: Exactly one claim (claim:3) had a verified timestamp and a substantive match above threshold; it wins by default eligibility.

claimA.evaluation_notes: Artifact consists solely of the generic placeholder phrase 'Hello World!' with no description of any repository, fork/clone workflow, teaching demo, or GitHub-specific structure. While the phrase loosely echoes the 'placeholder greeting' element mentioned in the disputed idea, it lacks any of the substantive mechanism, purpose, or context. This qualifies as superficial keyword overlap at best under the rubric. | [EXPECTED] Commit record content digest does not match the filed artifact

claimB.evaluation_notes: Artifact is the exact Spoon-Knife placeholder page (octocat fork prompt + forkit.gif) whose sole purpose is to demonstrate the fork/clone/edit workflow. This matches the disputed idea's description of a minimal, non-functional GitHub-published teaching repo containing only a fork-related greeting. No other mechanism or application code is present, satisfying the highest match tier.
